flagged.evidence: Step 1.2 says that whenever Xf is not identically zero and Y is nonzero somewhere, the term (Xf)Y does not vanish. On R, take X=d/dx, a nonconstant smooth bump f supported near 0, and a nonzero smooth vector field Y supported near 2. Then Xf is not identically zero and Y is nonzero somewhere, but (Xf)Y=0 everywhere. Thus the asserted condition is false and does not establish the refutation.

Step 1.1 says to “apply it to each coordinate function x^j.” But the bracket was defined as an operator on C^infinity(M), while x^j and the coefficient Y^j are generally only defined on the chart U. No restriction of the derivation to local functions, nor a global bump-function extension, is supplied before steps 1.1–2.1 use these expressions.

The hypothesis supplies equality only for global f in C^infinity(N), but step 1.2 concludes that dF_p(X_p) and Y_{F(p)} are equal derivations on C^infinity_{F(p)}(N). The cited definition of the differential acts on germs, not merely global functions. The missing localization argument that global smooth functions determine all tangent germs is not given.

After obtaining only a subsequence gamma(t_n)->q, step 2.1 says: “Applying [L1] at (b,q) gives a local solution starting from q ... and uniqueness patches it to gamma.” A local solution with initial value q at time b has no common initial value with gamma, which is defined only before b and merely has a subsequence converging to q. One must instead obtain a uniform local evolution neighbourhood and extend from gamma(t_n) for sufficiently large n; that argument is absent.

Step 1.2 treats f↦D(f)(p) as a derivation at p and invokes [L2]. But [L2]'s tangent vectors are derivations C_p^infinity(M)->R on germs, whereas D is only defined on C^infinity(M). The proof never establishes that D(f)(p) depends only on the germ of f. Consequently the application of [L2], and the later notation D(x^i) for chart-local coordinates, needs an omitted bump/localization argument.

Step 2.1 only arranges that a single local set O_p contains no repeated points from one local flow line. In step 3.1, two preimages may instead lie in distinct sets O_{p_1} and O_{p_2}; after showing p_2 lies on the orbit through p_1, the proof simply says that “the shrinkage in step 2.1 forces” equality. No compatible global shrinking is constructed, so injectivity of the union O=union_p O_p does not follow.

To prove that the maximal-flow domain is open, step 2.1 asserts: “For p near p_0, the point Phi(t_0,p) lies in U.” But Phi(t_0,p) is defined only when (t_0,p) is already in the domain D; establishing precisely that neighbourhood is the goal of the argument. The cited local theorem at q_0 supplies a flow near q_0, not existence of Phi(t_0,p) for nearby p. A finite continuation along gamma_{p_0} is required and is absent.
